reference.view_jobs: A relationship needs a structured view when the reader must follow how parts relate, not only what each is. The kinds, each with the view that carries it: hierarchy or belonging (a tree); a call path from an entry to its effect (a call path); ordered steps with evidence (a trace); ordered work with branches (a flowchart or flow); participants exchanging messages over time (a sequence diagram); states and transitions (a state diagram); boundaries, ownership and dependencies (a board with arrows); records, identity and cardinality (an entity diagram); numeric change across ordered categories (a chart); the same questions answered for several items (a table); alternatives on corresponding topics (a comparison); exact source, schema, configuration or commands the reader must inspect (a code view); a few headline numbers, each with its meaning and a comparison (stats); one named component, option or finding with its depth (a card). A simple fact or an interpretation needs no separate view: prose under a purposeful heading carries it. An answer-first summary that names a point the page explains, with its view, under a later heading leads with the answer and needs no view of its own.

reference.next_to: Next to means a reader finds the view where they read about its point: right before or after the passage that explains it, or after a short run of paragraphs on that same point. A run of points that one view draws together counts as one passage. A view is away from its text when it sits past unrelated points or other views, or so far from its passage, such as at the end of a long section, that the reader has to hunt for it.

reference.detail: Long detail sits one action away (a tab, a disclosure, a linked page) so nothing becomes a text wall. Optional depth is what a reader can skip and still follow the page's open questions and conclusions: history and earlier decisions, rationale, evidence, receipts, provenance such as exact quotes behind a summary, inventories, reference data, and trace or index tables that map items the page states in their own sections. That holds even when the table is the whole of its section. Content the reader needs in view stays: the exact corresponding facts a comparison or choice on the page rests on, a contract or core mapping the page is about, and failure cases with their thresholds that the page states nowhere else. A disclosure holds only the rationale or evidence about failure cases, never the cases themselves. Content carried from a source keeps its form and initial state; that can't be seen on the page.
